newsitem.title: USA: Local economy healthy, but slowing -- Richmond Fed.
newsitem.headline: Local economy healthy, but slowing -- Richmond Fed.

text.p: The fifth U.S. economic district is still growing at a healthy clip, but recent data suggest the economy might be slowing a bit, an official at the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond said.

"The reports that we were receiving do suggest an economy that is still growing at a fairly healthy clip, but one that is decelerating a little bit from the end of the first quarter," Richond Fed economist Raymond Owens said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Owens' comments came shortly after the Richmond Fed released its manufacturing survey for the month of April.
Owens also said regional manufacturing prices were growing at a slower pace than overall inflation in the region.
"Certainly we're seeing a bit of an uptick in price movements reported ... Now putting that into the context of inflation perhaps is a somewhat different punchline.
"It tells us that prices are moving up, but at levels less than the general level of inflation," Owens said.
Owens also said local manufacturing activity in the fifth region was slower in April versus the hot levels in March.
The economist added, however, that April figures are not necessarily much weaker when compared to the average growth rate registered in the entire first quarter.
"Certainly what our survey suggests in our district is that April growth was perhaps somewhat slower than March," Owens said.
"But remember March was only one month of the first quarter and we had a surge of activity here in March.

"So if you were to look at the average level of the first quarter and judge ... how that compares to the latest (survey) in April then I wouldn't say that April was necessarily slower than the first quarter," he added.
The Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond covers the country's fifth economic region, which includes the District of Columbia, Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia and most of West Virginia.
